counterevidence_considered.description: The dataset does contain repeated measurements of each independent unit (a June and a September DOC value per stream), which is the raw material for the issue class if a workflow were to enter both visits as separate trials; however, this workflow differences the pair into one signed change per stream before testing, so the repeated measurements never enter the sign test as separate observations.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: two DOC measurements per stream present in wide format; collapsed to one delta before testing

source_refs.quoted_text: The two visits to a stream are repeated measurements of the same unit, so the analysis first subtracts them into one signed change per stream and then tests those twenty-four changes. The paired values are never entered into the test as separate observations, and the number of trials in the test equals the number of streams.

Reads data/input.csv and writes results/report.md. Every catchment occupies
exactly one line of the source file, and the pair of visits belonging to a
stream is reduced to a single signed change before any test is run, so the
sample size of the test equals the number of independent catchments.

evidence.description: The input file contains exactly 24 data rows with 24 unique stream_code values (PG01 through PG24), so each independent unit occupies exactly one row and no unit is repeated in the file.

The data description designates stream_code as the independent-unit column, defines one trial as one row, and states the paired visits are stored side by side in a single record, so the wide layout keeps repeated measurements out of separate rows.
evidence.observed_value: independent unit = stream_code; one trial = one row; both visits in one record

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one proglacial stream, carrying its catchment descriptors together with its single June and its single September dissolved organic carbon measurement
Independent unit column: stream_code
One trial is: one row

The file `data/input.csv` holds one record per proglacial stream in a survey of glaciated headwater catchments in a single mountain range. Twenty-four streams were visited twice during the same melt year, early in the season (June) and late in the season (September). Both visit values sit side by side in the same record, so a stream never occupies more than one line of the file.

evidence.description: The workflow explicitly guards against duplicated independent units by raising an error if any stream_code repeats, then reduces each stream's two visits to one signed change so exactly one observation per unit enters the test.
evidence.observed_value: duplicate guard present; one delta per stream computed

source_refs.quoted_text:
changes = []
    for row in records:
        june = float(row["doc_june_mg_per_l"])
        sept = float(row["doc_sept_mg_per_l"])
        changes.append((row["stream_code"], sept - june))

evidence.description: The row-independent procedure (exact binomial sign test) is applied to the per-stream signs of change, with the number of trials derived from the list of per-stream changes, so the test's n equals the number of independent catchments (24), not the number of water samples (48).

source_refs.quoted_text:
n_units = len(changes)
    risers = sum(1 for _, delta in changes if delta > 0.0)
    fallers = sum(1 for _, delta in changes if delta < 0.0)
    ties = n_units - risers - fallers
    informative = risers + fallers

outcome = binomtest(risers, informative, 0.5, alternative="two-sided")
    p_value = outcome.pvalue

evidence.description: Independent recomputation from data/input.csv confirms the reported statistics: 18 of 24 streams show a positive September-minus-June change, 6 show a negative change, 0 ties, and the exact two-sided binomial p-value for 18/24 at null probability 0.5 is 2 * 190051/16777216 = 0.02266, matching the reported p = 0.0227 and n = 24.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- independent catchments analysed: 24
- streams with higher September DOC: 18
- streams with lower September DOC: 6
- ties excluded: 0
- proportion of streams increasing: 0.750
- exact two-sided p-value: 0.0227

[selected-result] Exact two-sided sign test (binomial test, null probability 0.5) on 24 independent proglacial catchments, one paired June-to-September change each: 18 of 24 streams had higher September dissolved organic carbon, proportion 0.750, p = 0.0227, so the 50/50 null is rejected at the 0.05 level.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the opposite verdict by searching for any mechanism through which a single stream could contribute more than one trial to the binomial test: (1) checked all 24 stream_code values in data/input.csv for duplicates (none; each code appears once); (2) inspected the workflow for any long-format expansion that would enter the June and September values as separate observations (none exists; the pair is subtracted into one delta per row before the test); (3) checked whether the test's n could reflect 48 water samples rather than 24 streams (it cannot; n_units = len(changes) = 24 and binomtest receives risers out of risers+fallers = 24); (4) recomputed all 24 deltas, the 18/6/0 split, and the exact two-sided binomial p-value (0.022656 ~ 0.0227), which match the report exactly. Every check failed to produce evidence of repeated independent-unit entry, supporting the no-issue verdict.
